rows.ARS:
Apricot or apricot blend Floribunda.
Registration name: JACgrant
Exhibition name: Fragrant Apricot ™
rows.Origin:
Bred by Dr. Keith W. Zary (United States, before 1998).
Introduced in United States by Bear Creek Gardens, Inc. in 1999 as 'Fragrant Apricot'.
rows.Bloom: Apricot, lighter edges. Strong, damask fragrance. 30 to 35 petals. Average diameter 4". Large, full (26-40 petals), cluster-flowered, in small clusters, high-centered to cupped, reflexed, rounded bloom form. Continuous (perpetual) bloom throughout the season. Long, pointed buds.
rows.Habit:
Medium, armed with thorns / prickles, upright, well-branched. Large, medium green, dense, leathery foliage.

Height: 3' to 42" (90 to 105cm). Width: 30" (75cm).
rows.Growing: USDA zone 6b and warmer. Can be used for beds and borders, container rose, cut flower or garden. Disease susceptibility: susceptible to blackspot . Spring Pruning: Remove old canes and dead or diseased wood and cut back canes that cross. In warmer climates, cut back the remaining canes by about one-third. In colder areas, you'll probably find you'll have to prune a little more than that. Requires spring freeze protection (see glossary - Spring freeze protection) . Can be grown in the ground or in a container (container requires winter protection).
